hero.title: File:Haisla canoe (UBC-2009).jpg
hero.description: This canoe was carved and painted by David Shant's assistants around 1934. The canoe was made by the native Indian Haisla members of the Kitimat Athlete club. It was donated as a gift to the UBC Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada in 1948...where it is displayed today.

gallery.title: File:Haida house pole (UBC-2009).jpg
gallery.description: This Haida house-front pole once stood before a dwelling named "Plenty of Ilimen-Hides in this House." It belonged to an Indian clan named 'Those Born at Qadasgo Creek.' It is now part of the UBC Museum of Anthropology's collection in Vancouver, Canada.

gallery.title: File:19th century Slovak jug (UBC-2009a).jpg
gallery.description: This is a c.1850 jug from Slovakia. This ceramic object is now located in the Koerner European Ceramic Gallery of UBC’s Museum of Anthropology. Its catalogue number is Cat 278.

gallery.title: File:19th century Holitsch dish (UBC).jpg
gallery.description: This is a circa 1746-1800 Holitsch dish from Slovakia. It is today located in the Koerner European Ceramic Gallery of UBC's Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada.

gallery.title: File:17th century Kendi pot (UBC).jpg
gallery.description: This Kendi (sprouted pot) dates from 1660 to 1685. The painted porcelain ware originates from Arita, Japan. It is today located in the Koerner European Ceramic Gallery of UBC’s Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada. Although the gallery focuses primarily on European art, it contains a generous collection of Asian art too including this object.

gallery.title: File:First Nations art objects UBC-2009.jpg
gallery.description: This is my picture of numerous diverse pieces of Canadian First Nations art work on display at UBC's Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada. Forefront piece is a feast dish in the shape of Dzunukwa.

gallery.title: File:1699 Odler dish (UBC).jpg
gallery.description: This 1699 dish comes from the Odler workshop in Dechtice, Slovakia. The Odlers were a family of craftsman who had converted to Catholicism from the Anabaptist community. This is one of their well known blue and white wares. It is today located in the Koerner European Ceramic Gallery of UBC's Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada. (Note: This image is a cropped version of my original full resolution picture.)

gallery.title: File:Arctic American shirt (UBC).jpg
gallery.description: This is a traditional Native Subarctic American shirt. It is today placed on permanent display within the collection of UBC's Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada.

gallery.title: File:Early 20th Century Micronesian Armour.jpg
gallery.description: This is an excellent example of early 20th century Micronesian Armour collected by Frank Burnett, a Canadian writer, in Kiribati in 1902. The armour is made of finely woven coir that covers the whole body and its breastplate is intriguingly made of stingray skin. The neck protector has rows of a diamond design pattern in black on dark brown ground. This item was donated to the UBC Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada, in 1927 where its museum catalogue number is C1491 a-e

gallery.title: File:Ndebele ornament (UBC 2013).jpg
gallery.description: This is a traditional Ndebele breast ornament from South Africa which is now part of the permanent collection of the UBC Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada. Green, black, white, purple, and blue beadwork decorates one side of the ornament. This item's museum catalogue number is Ab354.
categories: Taken with Canon PowerShot A590 IS

gallery.title: File:Ndebele cape (UBC 2013).jpg
gallery.description: This is an Ndebele cape from South Africa. This cape features geometric designs in black, white, blue, and green and is today part of the permanent collection of the UBC Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada, where its museum catalogue number is Ab351
categories: Taken with Canon PowerShot A590 IS

gallery.title: File:Olea Davis bowl (UBC 2013).jpg
gallery.description: This is an Olea Davis Canadian bowl now located within the UBC Museum of Anthropology in Vancouver, Canada, where its museum catalogue number is 2875/35. It was donated to the Museum of Anthropology in April 2011 and this bowl measures 17 cm by 3 cm. Olea Davis (1899-1977) was a leading figure of British Columbia pottery and is well known for her involvement in the ceramic programs held at UBC in the 1950's and 1960's. She co-founded the Pottery Guild of BC in 1955, an organization which supports BC's ceramic artists today.
categories: Taken with Canon PowerShot A590 IS
